previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with alcoholic and hepatitis C-related cirrhosis and a known 2.6 cm hepatocellular carcinoma was admitted for transarterial chemoembolization (TACE). The procedure was performed successfully via right femoral access with doxorubicin-loaded beads, and she recovered without complications. Post-procedure, she experienced expected abdominal cramping and transient symptoms of alcohol withdrawal, including headache and auditory hallucinations, which resolved with supportive care and detoxification protocol. Her mental status improved, and liver function remained stable despite a transient rise in AST. She was managed with pain control, continued cirrhosis medications, and psychiatric support. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans for MRI and ongoing liver and mental health care.

# Post-TACE Syndrome: 
Ms. ___ presented on ___ to ___ with abdominal 
pain, nausea and vomiting s/p TACE procedure on ___. The 
TACE procedure itself occurred due to patient's known HCC, with 
right common femoral artery access, and a second order LHA

hypodense lesion in segment II of the liver consistent with 
necrosis s/p TACE. In addition, the scan showed a 1.7 x 2.0 x 
1.7 cm hypodense focus in segment II corresponding to the recent 
TACE site (image 2:19). A patent umbilical vein was noted.  The 
portal vein was patent and the patient was seen to be s/p 
cholecystectomy. Evidence of mild colitis was seen in the bowel. 
The patient was admitted to ___ initially for concern of viral 
gastroenteritis, however symptoms were ultimately found to be 
more consistent with Post-TACE syndrome. Her diet was advanced 
as tolerated, her lactulose restarted, and her spironolactone 
restarted. Her condition continued to improve, and she was 
discharged home.
